title: Navigation API: Inconsistency between spec and tests about WaitForAll

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The spec uses a [#wait-for-all](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#commit-a-navigate-event:~:text=Wait%20for%20all%20of%20promisesList%2C%20with%20the%20following%20success%20steps) when running the intercept handlers, which [synchronously](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#waiting-for-all-promise:~:text=Perform%20failureSteps%20given%20arg%2E&text=If%20fullfilledCount%20equals%20total%2C%20then%20perform%20successSteps%20given%20result%2E) runs the success/failure steps. This is different from [#waiting-for-all-promise](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#waiting-for-all-promise), which queues success/failure into a promise.

However, [location-href-intercept-reject.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/b502dee59cd3ec5ddfbe84622a200541650fc945/navigation-api/ordering-and-transition/location-href-intercept-reject.html#L43-L45) seems to expect the navigateerror to run in a promise (it is queued after "promise microtask"), which I think is wrong. It should run before, because it's running sync with the rejected handler.

Chromium seems to use [#waiting-for-all-promise](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/navigation_api/navigate_event.cc;l=391;drc=ee500ed0974f48252c721fa53f41758b71309178).
